reviews.review:
The year is 2035, but you will not find any laser guns or spaceships in this game. What you will find, however, is the most authentic military shooter/simulation of all times.

Unlike CoD and BF, ArmA puts the focus on realism and player choice. You can play any style you want, there is a large selection of different infantry weapons (assault rifles, sniper rifles, machineguns, submachineguns, pistols, grenade- and missile launchers etc.), all fully customizable with a wide range of attachments.

Furthermore you can drive and command cars, trucks, SUVs, jeeps, APCs, tanks, heavy artillery, UAVs, UGVs, helicopters, airplanes, boats and even more, nothing is missing in this war. To stop your enemy, you can set up mines on roads, call in an airstrike or attach a scope on your rifle and shoot the enemy from a safe position two kilometers across the island. Any kind of playstyle is the right choice, as long as the enemy is eliminated.

Will you be the lone wolf, who takes over the 270.5 km² island by himself, will you lead a highly specialized squad into battle, or will you assume the role of the commander, with hundreds of units waiting for your instructions? Or will you create your very own missions in the easy to use, yet extremely powerful mission editor? The choice is yours. Of course, if you need to take a break from all the fighting and war, you can also pass the time racing karts or transporting vital supplies to your allies with specialized helicopters. Anything is possible in this gigantic sandbox of conflict.

Last but not least, the graphics are some of the best ever, the island is truly huge, yet still every leaf on every little flower in every patch of grass is rendered in high definition and sways realistically in the wind (or rotor wash), provided your computer is not too old. The graphics are fully scaleable, though, you probably won't need a machine for thousands of dollars.

And if you do like futuristic technology, the first part of the tutorial takes place in a simulated VR environment, also all weapons and combat vehicles are based on real-life prototypes, upgraded versions of existing tech as well as projects that were abandoned because they were too expensive to produce in the early 2000's. Also, cluster bombs are back, but always watch out for collateral damage. You want to win the hearts and minds of the population, don't you?
